syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Foot Prints Without feet Supp. Reader

topics.title: Tricki's condition and Mrs Pumphrey's indulgence

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Tricki's unhealthy condition at the start of the story and identify its causes.
Explain how Mrs Pumphrey's over-indulgence of Tricki worsens his health.

topics.title: The narrator's advice and the decision to hospitalise Tricki

concepts.learning_objective: State the narrator's advice on diet and exercise and what he meant by it.
Explain why the narrator insisted on taking Tricki away to his surgery.

topics.title: Tricki's recovery at the surgery

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how fasting, plain food and exercise cured Tricki without any medicine.
Describe how life with the pack of dogs changed Tricki's appetite and behaviour.

topics.title: Mrs Pumphrey's gifts and the narrator's temptation

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the gifts Mrs Pumphrey sent and appreciate the humour of who enjoyed them.
Evaluate the narrator's temptation to keep Tricki and his decision to return him.

topics.title: Tricki's return and the irony of the title

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Tricki's transformation and his reunion with Mrs Pumphrey.
Analyse why Mrs Pumphrey's phrase 'a triumph of surgery' is ironic.

topics.title: Vocabulary, character and theme

concepts.learning_objective: Use the meanings of words from the chapter's glossary in context.
Evaluate the narrator's character and the story's message about indulgence.

topics.title: Meeting Anil: flattery and lies

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the tricks of flattery, false names and lies the young thief uses to win Anil's confidence.
Explain why the narrator judges Anil an easy target and how that judgement proves mistaken.

topics.title: Life with Anil: work, learning and trust

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Anil's kindness and trust shape his relationship with the boy.
Explain how Anil earns his living as a writer and how this affects his money.
Interpret the narrator's early view of education as a means to get ahead.

topics.title: The theft and the missed train

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse the excuses the narrator gives himself for robbing a trusting man.
Interpret the narrator's unexplained hesitation at the railway station.

topics.title: A night in the rain and the decision to return

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the narrator's study of how different people react when robbed and why Anil's reaction would differ.
Compare the narrator's early and later thoughts about the value of education.
Trace how the lonely, rainy night leads the narrator to reconsider and return the money.

topics.title: The morning after: silent forgiveness

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Anil shows that he knows of the theft yet forgives the boy without a word.
Evaluate how trust and kindness bring about the thief's change of heart.
Identify the author of the story and the first-person point of view from which it is told.

topics.title: Fowler meets Ausable: a disappointing secret agent
topics.ncert_sections: Opening of the story (up to 'In that thought is drama')

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Ausable's appearance, accent and surroundings differ from the usual image of a secret agent.
Explain why Fowler, a young romantic writer, feels let down by his evening with Ausable.

topics.title: Max, the midnight visitor, and the missile report
topics.ncert_sections: From the light switched on to Max's demand for the report

concepts.learning_objective: Identify how Max is described, how he entered the room and why his presence gives Fowler a real thrill.
Explain what the report is about and why rival agents want it.

topics.title: Ausable's balcony story and the knock at the door
topics.ncert_sections: From the complaint about the balcony to Max climbing over the window-sill

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse how Ausable's detailed account makes the imaginary balcony convincing to Max.
Explain how Ausable uses the expected knock to frighten Max into leaving through the window.

topics.title: The twist ending and presence of mind
topics.ncert_sections: From Max's drop from the sill to 'there is no balcony'

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the surprise ending: the waiter at the door and the balcony that never existed.
Evaluate Ausable's presence of mind and the irony of an unarmed man defeating an armed spy.

topics.title: Vocabulary and language of the story

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the meanings of words from the chapter's glossary as used in the story.
Interpret descriptive expressions from the story and report its dialogue correctly.

topics.title: Horace Danby: a respectable man with a secret

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Horace Danby appears respectable to others while secretly being a thief.
Explain why Horace robs one safe every year and how he spends the money.

topics.title: The planned robbery at Shotover Grange

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the careful preparations Horace makes before breaking into Shotover Grange.
Explain how Horace's hay fever hinders him and gives away his presence.

topics.title: The lady in red and the deception

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse the subtle ways in which the young lady convinces Horace that she owns the house.
Interpret the arguments Horace uses to justify his stealing and to persuade the lady to let him go.

topics.title: The arrest and the irony of honour among thieves

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Horace is caught and why nobody believes his story.
Evaluate the irony of the ending and which saying about thieves the story illustrates.

topics.title: The mystery of the footprints and how Griffin became invisible

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the boys came to follow footprints that appeared without any visible feet.
Describe how Griffin made his body transparent and why he became a homeless wanderer.

topics.title: Griffin's adventures in the London store and at Drury Lane

concepts.learning_objective: Recount what Griffin did in the big London store and how he escaped from it.
Explain why Griffin went to Drury Lane and evaluate how he behaved there.

topics.title: Griffin's arrival at the inn in Iping

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Griffin's arrival at Iping caused curiosity and how he explained himself to Mrs Hall.
Interpret why Mrs Hall tolerated her guest and how his money troubles began.

topics.title: The curious episode in the study and the haunted furniture

concepts.learning_objective: Recount the burglary in the clergyman's study and why it seemed extraordinary.
Interpret the events in Griffin's room and Mrs Hall's superstitious reaction to them.

topics.title: The unmasking at the inn and the struggle with Jaffers

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Griffin revealed himself to the people in the bar.
Explain how the constable Jaffers tried to arrest Griffin and why he failed.
Evaluate Griffin as a brilliant scientist who misused his discovery.

topics.title: Childhood, collecting and a mother's support

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Ebright's lonely childhood led him to collect butterflies, rocks, fossils and coins with determination.
Explain how Ebright's mother encouraged his interest in learning.

topics.title: The Travels of Monarch X and butterfly tagging

concepts.learning_objective: Identify how the book The Travels of Monarch X opened the world of science to Ebright.
Explain why Ebright raised monarchs in his basement and why he lost interest in tagging them.

topics.title: Science fairs: losing, learning and real experiments

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the lesson Ebright learnt from losing at the seventh-grade county science fair.
Describe Ebright's eighth- and ninth-grade experiments on the viral disease and on viceroys and monarchs.

topics.title: The gold spots, the hormone and the theory of cell life

concepts.learning_objective: Trace Ebright's research on the purpose of the gold spots on a monarch pupa and the hormone they produce.
Explain Ebright's theory of how a cell reads the blueprint of its DNA and why it matters.

topics.title: Interests beyond science and the qualities of a scientist

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Ebright's other interests and the influence of his teacher Richard A. Weiherer.
Evaluate the qualities the author names as the ingredients in the making of a scientist.

topics.title: Matilda's discontent and the invitation to the ball

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Matilda is always unhappy with her modest life and how her husband differs from her.
Describe Matilda's reaction to the Minister's invitation and how the problem of the dress is solved.

topics.title: Borrowing the necklace and the night of the ball

concepts.learning_objective: Recount how Matilda solves the problem of having no jewel by borrowing from Mme Forestier.
Interpret Matilda's success at the ball and her hurried departure as signs of her character.

topics.title: The loss of the necklace and its replacement

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the steps the Loisels take to find the lost necklace and to buy time.
Explain how the Loisels raise money to replace the necklace and evaluate their decision to hide the loss.

topics.title: Ten years of poverty and hard work

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the hardships the Loisels accept in order to repay their debt.
Analyse how ten years of labour change Matilda's appearance and character.

topics.title: The final revelation, setting and message
topics.ncert_sections: Ending, Think about it, Talk about it

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the irony of Mme Forestier's revelation that the necklace was false.
Identify the author and the clues that show the story is set in France among French speakers.
Evaluate the story's message about pride, honesty and contentment.

topics.title: Bholi's childhood and neglect at home

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the accident and illness that shaped Bholi's appearance, speech and confidence as a child.
Explain how Bholi was neglected at home compared with her healthy, good-looking siblings.

topics.title: Why Bholi is sent to school

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the Tehsildar's advice led Ramlal to send a daughter to the new girls' school.
Interpret the mother's reasons for choosing Bholi, and only Bholi, to go to school.

topics.title: Bholi's first day at school and her teacher

concepts.learning_objective: Explain Bholi's fears about school and what made her feel she was going somewhere better than home.
Analyse how the teacher's kindness and praise helped Bholi begin to overcome her stammer.
Interpret the imagery that conveys Bholi's new hope after meeting her teacher.

topics.title: Bishamber's proposal and the wedding

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Bholi's parents accepted Bishamber's proposal despite its drawbacks.
Evaluate Bishamber's demand for dowry and Ramlal's response at the wedding.

topics.title: Bholi's refusal and her transformation into Sulekha

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse why and how Bholi rejected the marriage at the wedding ceremony.
Evaluate Bholi's transformation and the teacher's role, including the significance of the name Sulekha.

chapters.title: The Book That Saved the Earth

topics.title: The Historian's introduction: the Era of the Book

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how the Historian describes the twentieth century and the Martian invasion of 2040.
Explain how the Historian and the historiscope frame the events of the play.

topics.title: Think-Tank and Noodle at Mars Space Control

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the vanity, arrogance and impatience of Think-Tank from his words and actions.
Describe Noodle's humble, obedient manner towards Think-Tank.

topics.title: The crew in the library: books as hats and sandwiches

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the wrong guesses the Martians make about the library and its books.
Explain the humour of the crew passing on Think-Tank's order to eat the 'sandwich'.

topics.title: Communication sandwiches, the code and the vitamins

concepts.learning_objective: Trace how Think-Tank's theory of 'communication sandwiches' and the 'code' develops.
Analyse how Noodle corrects Think-Tank's mistakes without offending him.

topics.title: Nursery rhymes misread as threats

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret how Think-Tank reads innocent nursery rhymes as threats from Earth.
Explain why the Humpty Dumpty rhyme makes Think-Tank abandon the invasion and flee.

topics.title: The Historian's epilogue and the play's message

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how relations between Earth and Mars stand in the twenty-fifth century.
Evaluate the play's irony and use words from the chapter's glossary correctly.
